name: MS-01
label: Safe R

key_factors: District's R+18 partisan lean anchors the seat firmly in Republican hands
Incumbent Trent Kelly holds a large cash advantage ($864K to $150K) after raising over $1M
Polymarket prices Kelly near 95% to win
No public polls or expert ratings cover the race; challenger fundraising is modest
model.rationale: An eighteen-point Republican district plus a renominated, well-funded incumbent leaves Democrat Cliff Johnson with almost no room, and betting markets corroborate a comfortable Kelly win.
model.watch: A wave of outside spending against Kelly or a sharp late shift in the national environment would be the main things that could loosen this rating.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Trent Kelly, the Republican incumbent, seeks another term in a northeast Mississippi district that has leaned heavily Republican for years, with a partisan lean of roughly eighteen points. He was renominated without difficulty and enters the general election with about $864,000 on hand after raising just over $1 million. Democrat Cliff Johnson has raised about $551,000, with $150,000 remaining.

No public polls or expert ratings cover the race, so the picture rests on the district's fundamentals. Betting markets give Kelly roughly a 95% chance of winning. Johnson's fundraising shows some local energy, but it is unlikely to overcome the structural margin in a low-profile contest. The forecast expects Kelly to win comfortably, and the seat is rated Safe Republican.
